title: Convexity of ordered prefix-union polynomials
subtitle: A moment representation for the full hypergraph convexity conjecture
blocks: Draft manuscript for MathDB 347913 | 1 November 2026 | No author attribution assigned

For every complete L-uniform hypergraph on n vertices and every integer degree d, we identify the polynomial with ordered prefix-union denominators as the dth moment of a random nonnegative linear form, divided by d!. The random coefficients are minima of independent rate-one exponential clocks. A labelled chamber decomposition proves the coefficient identity, including repeated edges. Scalar power convexity then proves convexity on the nonnegative orthant and hence on the sum-one simplex. This proves the full mathematical statement of Conjecture 1 of Brosch, Laurent and Steenkamp, without a degree ceiling or an L <= n restriction. We give all integrability and change-of-variable details and a correspondence with the accompanying unchanged Lean certificate.

The mathematical theorem below is asserted in full scope. Literature priority remains qualified: the completed ordinary review found no demonstrated earlier full subsumer within its bounded investigation, but left the 1967 Marshall-Olkin mgf body and a 2025 quantum-channel citing body unread. Let n, L, d be arbitrary integers at least two. Write [n] = {1,...,n}, let E be the set of all L-element subsets of [n], and put m = |E|. A weight vector x is a real-valued function on E. Every sum over E to the dth power below is over ordered tuples with repetition. For a tuple e = (e_1,...,e_d), define its inclusive prefix unions U_j(e).

Each nonempty tuple has |U_j(e)| >= L > 0. There is no factorial or multinomial coefficient in this definition. If L > n, E is empty, the polynomial is zero for d >= 2, and the sum-one simplex is empty. No barycenter is assigned when m = 0.

title: The theorem and the probability space
blocks: For every n, L, d >= 2, the function f_d is convex on the nonnegative orthant in the real vector space of functions on E. In particular it is convex on Delta_E: for all x,y in Delta_E and every theta in [0,1],

The simplex assertion is precisely MathDB 347913, using its source to define E and the simplex. It is arXiv:2009.04510v1, equation (2), Section 3, Conjecture 1, and SIAM J. Optim. 31(3) (2021), equation (1.1), Section 4, Conjecture 1, p. 2242 [1]. The theorem quantifies over all three integers with no finite parameter ceiling. The orthant assertion is a proof consequence and carries no separate result credit.

Use Omega = [0,infinity)^n with its Borel sigma-algebra and the product probability measure whose density is exp(-sum_v t_v) with respect to n-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Let T_v be the coordinate functions. They are independent rate-one exponentials. For every e in E define Z_e = min over v in e of T_v. Finite minima of coordinate functions are continuous and measurable, and Z_e >= 0 everywhere on this space. Repeated appearances of an edge always use this same random variable.

For every integer r >= 0, direct integration gives E[T_v^r] = integral from zero to infinity of t^r exp(-t) dt = r!. At r = 0 the integral is one. For r >= 1, integration by parts gives r times the preceding integral; t^r exp(-t) tends to zero at infinity, for example by bounding the exponential below by a larger-degree term of its power series. This also proves convergence.

The first inequality follows from scalar convexity of t to the rth power on nonnegative reals, applied to the average of the n clocks (equality for r = 1). Hence S has every finite integer moment. For any tuple e and k >= 1, (product_i Z_{e_i})^k <= S^(dk), since every lifetime lies between zero and S. The functions involved are measurable finite products and sums, so these dominations prove absolute integrability of all mixed products, their integer powers, and A_x^r for every signed real vector x. The zero powers are the constant one. If E is empty, A_x = 0 and the conclusions are immediate. Thus no formal convention for a divergent integral is used.

title: Joint survival and the layer-cake formula
blocks: Fix any ordered tuple e in E^d, allowing repeated edges. For t in the nonnegative orthant of R^d and a vertex v, let h_v(e,t) be the largest threshold among coordinates whose edges contain v, together with the baseline zero.

Proof. Each event Z_{e_i} > t_i says T_v > t_i for every v in e_i. Their intersection imposes the single maximal threshold at each vertex which appears in some tuple edge. At absent vertices the baseline zero imposes no probability cost, since T_v > 0 almost surely. Independence multiplies the tails exp(-h_v), giving the formula. Weak inequalities give the same probability: the finite union of events T_v = t_i has probability zero, since the clocks have densities. The h_v are finite maxima of continuous coordinate functions and zero, so the survival integrand is measurable. No independence between the Z_e is asserted. QED.

Proof. For any nonnegative finite numbers z_1,...,z_d, the product of their lengths is the Lebesgue volume of the box product_i (0,z_i]. Thus product_i z_i equals the integral over (0,infinity)^d of product_i 1_{t_i <= z_i}. Apply this equality to z_i = Z_{e_i}. The subset {(omega,t): 0 < t_i <= Z_{e_i}(omega) for every i} is measurable, because coordinate evaluations and the lifetimes are measurable. Its indicator is nonnegative. Tonelli on the product of the finite clock probability measure and sigma-finite Lebesgue measure permits interchange of integrals without a preliminary integrability assumption. Lemma 2 supplies the inner probability. The domination in Section 2 then shows that the resulting integral is finite. QED.

The variables t_i here are independent integration coordinates, not samples of the lifetimes. Even if e_i = e_j, the coordinates t_i and t_j remain distinct labels. Their equality hyperplane is null for d-dimensional volume; equality of the associated lifetimes need not be a probability-null event. This distinction is essential for the next step.

title: Labelled chambers and positive gaps
blocks: Let pi be a permutation of {1,...,d}. Define the strict descending chamber C_pi by t_{pi(1)} > ... > t_{pi(d)} > 0. Then

Proof. Every positive vector with distinct coordinates belongs to exactly one such chamber, by sorting its coordinate labels in descending order. The chambers are measurable, pairwise disjoint, and exhaust the positive orthant outside the finite union of hyperplanes t_i = t_j. Each hyperplane is Lebesgue-null: fixing all coordinates except t_i leaves a singleton in the remaining coordinate, and Tonelli gives zero volume on each bounded box; countably many boxes cover R^d. Coordinate-zero boundary hyperplanes are null as well. There are exactly d! labelled chambers, regardless of any equalities among edge values.
In C_pi set t_{pi(d+1)} = 0 as a boundary convention and introduce gaps:

These formulas are mutually inverse by telescoping. Strict descending positive coordinates correspond exactly to u_j > 0 for every j; the last gap is t_{pi(d)}, not a discarded coordinate. In the ordered t coordinates the inverse matrix has entries 1 if i <= j and 0 otherwise. It is upper triangular with diagonal one, so its determinant is one. The additional coordinate permutation has absolute determinant one. Both maps are invertible linear, hence Borel, and the ordinary linear change-of-variable theorem transports Lebesgue measure with Jacobian one.

For a vertex v appearing in some tuple edge, let k be its first position among e_{pi(1)},...,e_{pi(d)}. The largest threshold involving v is t_{pi(k)} = sum_{j >= k} u_j. Also v belongs to the prefix union through j exactly when j >= k. An absent vertex contributes zero on both sides. Summing these identities over all vertices and interchanging two finite sums yields

This proves the prefix orientation: a vertex contributes to all gaps at or after its first appearance. The transformed nonnegative integrand is product_j exp(-a_j u_j). Tonelli factors its integral into d integrals from zero to infinity. Each is 1/a_j by elementary integration of the exponential. All rates are strictly positive, so the factored integral is finite and is the claimed coefficient. QED.

title: Coefficient identification and convexity
blocks: For every real vector x on E, including signed vectors, the following identity holds:
Proof. Lemmas 3 and 4 and the null-set partition give the mixed-moment identity

The dth power of a finite sum expands as a sum over every ordered d-tuple. Every term is absolutely integrable by Section 2, even when its constant weight is negative. Taking expectation term by term is therefore legitimate. Substitute the mixed-moment formula and interchange the two finite sums to obtain

For fixed pi, the map e -> (e_{pi(1)},...,e_{pi(d)}) is a bijection on the full tuple space E^d, with inverse given by pi inverse. It preserves the product of weights by commutativity. Thus each inner sum equals f_d(x), including tuples with repeated values. There are d! permutations. This proves the displayed identity for signed weights, rather than only for nonnegative weights. QED.

If all tuple edges equal one edge e, each prefix has cardinality L, so c(e,...,e) = L^(-d). The symmetrized coefficient is d!/L^d; it is not L^(-d) after quotienting by the stabilizer. Independently P(Z_e > t) = exp(-Lt), and integration by parts (or the one-dimensional moment integral with s = Lt) gives E[Z_e^d] = d!/L^d. This verifies both the factorial direction and the repeated-edge convention. It is a symbolic control, not a numerical argument.

Take x,y >= 0 and theta in [0,1]. For every clock outcome A_x,A_y >= 0, and A_{theta x+(1-theta)y} = theta A_x+(1-theta)A_y. On the nonnegative half-line the function s -> s^d is convex: for d >= 2 its second derivative is d(d-1)s^(d-2) >= 0 on the positive half-line, and continuity extends the convexity inequality to zero. Apply it to these two linear forms and take expectations. All three powers are integrable by Section 2. Proposition 5 and division by d! > 0 give the claimed inequality for f_d. The nonnegative orthant is convex; the additional linear condition sum x_e = 1 defines a convex subset. Restriction proves the simplex claim. If L > n that subset is empty, so the quantified convexity assertion is vacuous. QED.
The signed-weight identity is not used to assert odd-power convexity on all real space. Nonnegativity is an explicit hypothesis in the pointwise convexity argument.

title: Relation to the source and the literature
blocks: Brosch, Laurent and Steenkamp [1] study two different classes. Their polynomial p_d uses only the final union cardinality as denominator. Its full convexity theorem is not a theorem about the successive prefix-union products defining f_d. For d = 2 one has f_2 = p_2/L; this relation does not remove the intermediate denominators at higher degrees. Their published Section 4 retains general f_d convexity as Conjecture 1, while proving degree three for L = 2. Our coefficient identification addresses those intermediate denominators directly.

Polak [2], Theorem 1.1 in the inspected arXiv v2 body, proves L = 2 and d <= 9, for all n. The reduction writes the Hessian as a sum of monomials times matrices indexed by multigraphs with d-2 edges; for each fixed d it reduces positive semidefiniteness for all n to finitely many constant matrices. The stated verification reaches d <= 9. This is not a general-degree or general-L theorem. The CWI PDF retrieved under the older review's label 'polak-published' is byte-identical to the arXiv preprint; it does not provide an independently inspected typeset journal body. The published metadata is SIAM J. Discrete Math. (2022), DOI 10.1137/21M1413298. We rely on the actual v2 theorem/proof context, not on the label of that cached file.

Brosch's 2022 thesis [3], Chapter 5, Conjecture 5.17, again states general convexity and develops the Hessian coefficient-matrix reduction. Cardinaels, Borst and van Leeuwaarden [4], in the inspected arXiv v2 body, relate light-traffic queue comparisons to coefficients alpha_q via Theorem 1 and Lemma 3. The discussion preceding Corollary 1 invokes Polak for q <= 9 and describes larger q as numerical support. That body does not supply the general moment identity proved here. These observations locate the result relative to specific inspected bodies; they do not claim exhaustive later-literature coverage.
4. Classical antecedent and explicit priority limit

The probability model is a special case of the classical Marshall-Olkin common-shock construction [5]. To see the identification directly, assign vertex v the set S_v = {e in E : v in e}. The independent clock T_v is a shock that kills exactly these edge lifetimes. Each edge survives until the first shock involving it, which is precisely min_{v in e} T_v. Equal S_v can be grouped by adding their rates. The resulting survival exponent is the sum, over shocks, of the largest threshold of their affected lifetimes. This is antecedent methodology; no new distribution is claimed.
